title: Injective abelian sheaves on a site have trivial higher Cech cohomology
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal I$ an injective object of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Then for every covering $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ of $\mathcal C$ the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] satisfies $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for all $p>0$ (and $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=\mathcal I(U)$). (General-site version of [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-cech-acyclic], which is stated for the small etale site; its proof is the same: $\mathcal I$ is injective in $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ (Lemma 03F6, sheafification being an exact left adjoint of the inclusion), and $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\textit{PAb}}(\mathbf Z_{\mathcal U,\bullet},\mathcal I)$ with $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal U,\bullet}$ exact in positive degrees.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech) and its proof (Lemma Tag 03F6 lemma-injective-abelian-sheaf-injective-presheaf, Lemma Tag 03AU lemma-cech-cohomology-derived-presheaves, Lemma Tag 03AN lemma-cech-h0)

proof.text: Write PAb(C) for presheaves of abelian groups and let I be the given injective sheaf. The inclusion Ab(C) into PAb(C) has sheafification as an exact left adjoint: finite limits are sectionwise and sheafification preserves finite limits and colimits. Therefore an extension problem from a monomorphism of presheaves into I sheafifies to an extension problem between sheaves, which is solved by injectivity of I; composing the extension with the unit of sheafification gives an extension in presheaves. Thus I is injective in PAb(C).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F6 (injective sheaf is injective presheaf)

proof.text: Let K_p be the direct sum of the free presheaves Z_{U_t0 x_U ... x_U U_tp} over tuples of covering indices, with alternating face differential. At an object W, decompose K_p(W) by the composite phi: W -> U. The summand for phi is the free abelian group on S_phi^(p+1), where S_phi is the disjoint union of lifts W -> U_t over phi. Face maps delete one entry. If S_phi is empty the summand is zero; otherwise choosing s in S_phi gives the contracting homotopy (s0,...,sp) -> (s,s0,...,sp) in positive degrees. Hence K is exact in every positive degree as a presheaf.

source.place: Lemmas Tags 03AS and 03AT (free Cech complex and contracting homotopy)

proof.text: For every presheaf G, Yoneda identifies Hom(Z_V,G) with G(V), naturally in V and G. Hom out of a direct sum is a product, so Hom(K_p,G) is the product of G on the iterated fibre products; precomposition with a face is restriction along the corresponding projection. The resulting cochain differential is exactly the Cech differential, so Hom(K,I) is the Cech complex of I.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AS (Cech complex as Hom from the free complex)

proof.text: For p>0, a cocycle s: K_p -> I vanishes on im(d_{p+1}) = ker(d_p), hence factors through B = im(d_p) included in K_{p-1}. Injectivity of I in presheaves extends B -> I to K_{p-1} -> I, whose composite with d_p is s. Every positive-degree cocycle is therefore a coboundary, and Cech H^p(U,I)=0.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AW via the second paragraph of Lemma Tag 03AU

proof.text: In degree zero, a Cech cocycle is a section of I(U) whose restrictions to every pairwise fibre product agree. The sheaf condition identifies these compatible families with the unique section on U, giving Cech H^0(U,I)=I(U).

split_report.summary: Split the general-site statement along Stacks 03AW. The proof first transfers injectivity from sheaves to presheaves through the exact sheafification adjunction, then constructs the free Cech presheaf complex and proves its positive-degree exactness by decomposing each value into contractible complexes on the sets of lifts over a fixed map to U. Yoneda identifies Hom from this complex with the Cech complex, and injectivity makes every positive cocycle a coboundary. The sheaf equalizer condition gives the degree-zero identification. The proof uses only the general site and Cech definitions; no small-etale specialization or new node was introduced. Mathlib searches found no Cech-acyclicity theorem for injective sheaves.
